newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's SPD party says Bewag stake to be sold.
newsitem.headline: Germany's SPD party says Bewag stake to be sold.

text.p: A political party in Berlin said on Monday that a majority stake in the German power utility Berliner Kraft und Licht AG (BEWAG) would be sold for 2.9 billion marks ($1.7 billion) to a German-U.S. consortium.
The Social Democratic Party (SPD) said the 50.8 percent stake would be sold but SPD regional party leader Klaus Hartung declined to name the buyers.
But the stake was widely expected to be sold to German utility groups VIAG AG and Veba AG and U.S. utility Southern Co since Veba and VIAG each currently hold a 10 percent stake in BEWAG.

The deal is expected to give Atlanta-based Southern, one of the largest utilities in the United States, a 23.6 percent stake in the utility, while Veba and VIAG will also both raise their individual stakes to 23.6 percent.
Berlin's city-state parliament was expected to approve the deal on Tuesday.
Germany's federal cartel office has already expressed an opinion that it was against Veba raising its stake in BEWAG, saying its stake would be too extensive.
But German media reports have said Southern was expected to be formally in charge of the commercial management of BEWAG although all decisions would be reached jointly.
